title: Charles Darwin: Greatest Scientist of All Time?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: the gradual change of species over time.
the process where organisms with helpful traits survive and reproduce.
a group of similar organisms that can reproduce together.
an earlier living form from which others evolved.
a feature that helps an organism survive in its environment.
preserved remains or traces of ancient life.
a scientific explanation based on evidence.

sentences.en: In the 19th century, a quiet, curious naturalist named Charles Darwin proposed a theory that went on the shake science, religion, and philosophy.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪，一位安静、好奇的博物学家名叫Charles Darwin，他提出了一项震撼科学界、宗教界和哲学的理论。

sentences.en: Darwin introduced a new way of thinking about life itself.
sentences.zh: Darwin引入了一种思考生命本身的新方式。

sentences.en: His theory of evolution by natural selection revealed that every species (humans included) changes over time, adapts to its environment, and shares common ancestors.
sentences.zh: 他的自然选择进化论揭示了：每一个物种（包括人类）都在随着时间推移而改变，适应其环境，并且拥有共同的祖先。

sentences.en: In today’s episode of Thinking in English, I want to explore the life of Charles Darwin, look closely at his most important discoveries, and discuss how his ideas still influence modern biology.
sentences.zh: 在今天的Thinking in English节目中，我想探讨Charles Darwin的一生，仔细研究他最重要的发现，并讨论他的思想如何依然影响着现代生物学。

sentences.en: And finally, we’ll discuss a big question: Is Charles Darwin the greatest scientist of all time?
sentences.zh: 最后，我们要讨论一个重大问题：Charles Darwin是有史以来最伟大的科学家吗？

sentences.en: And while we are doing this, we’ll practice our English listening comprehension and learn some new English vocabulary!
sentences.zh: 在探讨这些的同时，我们还将练习英语听力理解并学习一些新的英语词汇！

sentences.en: Charles Darwin was born in 1809 in Shrewsbury.
sentences.zh: Charles Darwin于1809年出生在Shrewsbury。

sentences.en: Shrewsbury is a quiet market town in western England.
sentences.zh: Shrewsbury是英格兰西部一个安静的集镇。

sentences.en: He grew up in a comfortable and wealthy family home surrounded by books and learning.
sentences.zh: 他在一个舒适且富裕的家庭环境中长大，四周环绕着书籍和知识。

sentences.en: His parents had expectations that he would become a doctor like his father.
sentences.zh: 他的父母期望他能像他父亲一样成为一名医生。

sentences.en: Or perhaps a clergyman in the Church of England.
sentences.zh: 或者也许成为英国国教会的一名神职人员。

sentences.en: These were both respectable careers for a young man of his background.
sentences.zh: 对于他这种背景的年轻人来说，这两者都是受人尊敬的职业。

sentences.en: But young Darwin had different interests.
sentences.zh: 但年轻的Darwin有着不同的兴趣。

sentences.en: At medical school in Edinburgh, he quickly discovered that he hated the sight of surgery.
sentences.zh: 在爱丁堡的医学院里，他很快发现自己极其讨厌看到手术的血腥场面。

sentences.en: Remember, Darwin was alive in the 19th century and he was at medical school at a time before painkillers and before anesthesia.
sentences.zh: 记住，Darwin生活在19世纪，他上医学院的那个年代还没有止痛药和麻醉剂。

sentences.en: Operations were painful and brutal, and Darwin soon realized that the medical profession wasn’t for him.
sentences.zh: 手术过程痛苦且残忍，Darwin很快意识到医学行业并不适合他。

sentences.en: Eventually, he moved to Cambridge to prepare for a career in the church.
sentences.zh: 最终，他搬到了Cambridge，为从事教会职业做准备。

sentences.en: Ironically, it was while studying theology, studying religion, at Cambridge University, not while he was a medical school student, that he discovered a passion for science and studying nature.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，正是在Cambridge大学学习神学、研究宗教期间，而不是在当医学院学生时，他发现了自己对科学和自然研究的热情。

sentences.en: Darwin loved collecting insects, examining rocks, and learning about the natural world.
sentences.zh: Darwin热爱收集昆虫、检查岩石以及了解自然界。

sentences.en: He spent hours looking for plants and animals and was far more interested in beetles than in theology.
sentences.zh: 他花了好几个小时寻找动植物，对甲虫的兴趣远远超过了神学。

sentences.en: At Cambridge, he also met John Henslow, a respected botanist and professor.
sentences.zh: 在Cambridge，他还结识了John Henslow，一位备受尊敬的植物学家兼教授。

sentences.en: Henslow recognized Darwin’s curiosity and encouraged him to pursue his interests and study nature.
sentences.zh: Henslow发现了Darwin的好奇心，并鼓励他追求自己的兴趣去研究自然。

sentences.en: When he was 22 years old, Charles Darwin received an invitation to join a global expedition aboard a British Navy ship called HMS Beagle.
sentences.zh: 22岁时，Charles Darwin收到了一份邀请，登上了一艘名为HMS Beagle的英国海军舰艇，参与环球考察。

sentences.en: This was thanks to the recommendation of his mentor, John Henslow.
sentences.zh: 这要归功于他的导师John Henslow的推荐。

sentences.en: His role on the ship was the ship’s naturalist.
sentences.zh: 他在船上的角色是船上的博物学家。

sentences.en: He was responsible for observing, collecting, and recording plants, animals, rocks, and fossils along the journey.
sentences.zh: 他负责在旅途中观察、收集和记录动植物、岩石以及化石。

sentences.en: For five years, the Beagle traveled around the world, stopping in South America, Australia, Africa, and many small islands.
sentences.zh: 历时五年，Beagle号环游世界，停靠在南美洲、澳大利亚、非洲以及许多小岛上。

sentences.en: When the ship stopped at a port, Darwin would spend a lot of time exploring the new landscapes, talking to local people, and carefully collecting specimens.
sentences.zh: 当船停靠在港口时，Darwin会花大量时间探索新的地貌、与当地人交谈，并仔细收集标本。

sentences.en: Gradually he noticed things that changed the way he understood nature and life.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，他注意到了一些事情，这些事情改变了他对自然和生命的理解。

sentences.en: In South America, Darwin found or was shown fossils from large extinct animals, such as giant armadillo-like creatures.
sentences.zh: 在南美洲，Darwin发现了或者有人向他展示了大型灭绝动物的化石，例如类似巨型犰狳的生物。

sentences.en: These fossils closely resembled, looked very similar to, smaller animals still living in the region.
sentences.zh: 这些化石与该地区仍然生活着的小型动物高度相似，外形非常接近。

sentences.en: The fossils were similar, but not identical to modern species.
sentences.zh: 这些化石虽然相似，但与现代物种并不完全相同。

sentences.en: Why? Why would extinct animals look like larger versions of living ones?
sentences.zh: 为什么呢？为什么灭绝的动物会长得像现存动物的放大版？

sentences.en: Darwin suspected that there was a possible connection between these animals over time.
sentences.zh: Darwin怀疑随着时间的推移，这些动物之间可能存在某种联系。

sentences.en: He started to consider that species might change rather than remain fixed forever.
sentences.zh: 他开始认为物种可能会发生变化，而不是永远保持不变。

sentences.en: Darwin also observed unusual patterns among living animals.
sentences.zh: Darwin还观察到活体动物之间一些不寻常的模式。

sentences.en: In Patagonia, he encountered a type of flightless bird called a Rhea, similar to an ostrich.
sentences.zh: 在巴塔哥尼亚，他遇到了一种不会飞的鸟，叫做Rhea（美洲鸵），类似于鸵鸟。

sentences.en: However, he noticed that one Rhea species lived further south while a slightly different species lived further north.
sentences.zh: 然而，他注意到一种Rhea生活在更靠南的地方，而另一种略有不同的Rhea生活在更靠北的地方。

sentences.en: Again, the question arose: Why would these closely related animals live in different regions and have slightly different appearances?
sentences.zh: 问题再次出现：为什么这些亲缘关系密切的动物会生活在不同的地区，并且外观略有不同？

sentences.en: In Chile, Darwin witnessed a very powerful earthquake.
sentences.zh: 在智利，Darwin亲历了一场非常强烈的地震。

sentences.en: The earthquake lifted parts of the land several meters high.
sentences.zh: 地震将部分陆地抬高了数米高。

sentences.en: This dramatic event revealed to Darwin that the earth is not static.
sentences.zh: 这一戏剧性的事件向Darwin揭示了地球并不是静止的。

sentences.en: The earth changes over periods of time, and sometimes this change can happen suddenly.
sentences.zh: 地球在一段时间内会发生变化，有时这种变化会突然发生。

sentences.en: If the land could transform over time, perhaps life could change too.
sentences.zh: 如果陆地能随时间改变，也许生命也能改变。

sentences.en: But the most influential moment of the voyage came on the Galapagos Islands, a volcanic island group near the equator.
sentences.zh: 但这次航行中最具影响力的时刻发生在Galapagos群岛，这是一群靠近赤道的火山岛。

sentences.en: The islands were home to animals, found nowhere else in the world.
sentences.zh: 这些岛屿上生活着世界上其他地方找不到的动物。

sentences.en: Darwin studied finches, small birds with surprisingly diverse beak shapes.
sentences.zh: Darwin研究了雀类（finches），这是一种喙部形状出奇多样的小鸟。

sentences.en: On one island, finches had strong, thick beaks for cracking seeds.
sentences.zh: 在一个岛上，雀类拥有强壮而厚实的喙，用来砸开种子。

sentences.en: On a different island, finches has had longer, more delicate beaks ideal for eating insects or cactus nectar.
sentences.zh: 在另一个不同的岛上，雀类拥有更长、更精致的喙，非常适合吃昆虫或仙人掌花蜜。

sentences.en: Similarly, the giant tortoises on each island had different shell shapes, and locals could often identify a tortoise’s island simply by looking at its shell.
sentences.zh: 同样，每个岛上的巨龟都有不同的外壳形状，当地人通常只需看一眼龟壳就能认出乌龟来自哪个岛。

sentences.en: These details might seem small, but for Darwin, they raised some important questions.
sentences.zh: 这些细节可能看起来微不足道，但对Darwin而言，它们引发了一些重要的问题。

sentences.en: Could different environments shape the bodies and behaviors of living creatures over time?
sentences.zh: 不同的环境会不会随着时间的推移塑造生物的身体和行为？

sentences.en: Darwin began to suspect that species change gradually over time.
sentences.zh: Darwin开始怀疑物种随时间在逐渐变化。

sentences.en: They adapt to the specific conditions of their environment.
sentences.zh: 它们适应了各自环境的具体条件。

sentences.en: The Beagle voyage provided the observations, the evidence, and the inspiration that would eventually lead Darwin to the revolutionary Theory of Evolution.
sentences.zh: Beagle号的航行为Darwin提供了最终带来革命性进化论的观察结果、证据和灵感。

sentences.en: After returning to England in 1836, Darwin did not publish his ideas, at least not immediately.
sentences.zh: 1836年返回英格兰后，Darwin并没有立即发表他的想法，至少没有马上发表。

sentences.en: He spent more than 20 years studying plants, animals, fossils, geology, and as many scientific papers as possible.
sentences.zh: 他花了20多年的时间研究植物、动物、化石、地质学，以及尽可能多的科学论文。

sentences.en: He filled notebooks with his observations and questions and ideas.
sentences.zh: 他的笔记本上记满了观察结果、问题和想法。

sentences.en: Rather than rushing to conclusions, Darwin took his time.
sentences.zh: Darwin没有急于得出结论，而是从容不迫。

sentences.en: He built a mountain of evidence to support his theory.
sentences.zh: 他积累了如山的证据来支持他的理论。

sentences.en: He knew that evolution was going to be a controversial theory, so he wanted as much evidence as possible to support it.
sentences.zh: 他知道进化论将是一个备受争议的理论，所以他希望有尽可能多的证据来支持它。

sentences.en: Darwin studied the work of geologists like Charles Lyell.
sentences.zh: Darwin研究了像Charles Lyell等地质学家的著作。

sentences.en: Lyell’s work argued that the earth had changed gradually over incredibly long periods of time.
sentences.zh: Lyell的著作论证了地球在极其漫长的时间里发生了渐进式的改变。

sentences.en: Mountains rose, oceans retreated and landscapes were shaped by these slow processes.
sentences.zh: 山脉隆起，海洋退去，地貌正是由这些缓慢的过程塑造的。

sentences.en: If the earth was ancient and always changing, then the life living on earth might also change as well.
sentences.zh: 如果地球是古老的且一直在变化，那么生活在地球上的生命也可能会发生改变。

sentences.en: Darwin also studied selective breeding, which is a process used by farmers and animal breeders.
sentences.zh: Darwin还研究了人工选择，这是农民和动物育种者使用的一种方法。

sentences.en: For centuries, humans have known that choosing animals or plants with desirable traits like bigger cows or sweeter apples or faster horses, and then breeding them can change future generations.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，人类一直知道，选择具有理想特征的动植物——比如更大的奶牛、更甜的苹果或跑得更快的马——然后进行繁育，就能改变后代。

sentences.en: If humans could influence how animals and plants change, then perhaps nature could do something similar on its own, without human control.
sentences.zh: 如果人类能够影响动植物的变化方式，那么大自然也许也能靠自己做出类似的事情，而无需人类控制。

sentences.en: A final key influence came from reading Thomas Malthus.
sentences.zh: 最后一个关键影响来自阅读Thomas Malthus的著作。

sentences.en: Malthus wrote that populations grow faster than the food supply.
sentences.zh: Malthus写道，人口增长的速度快于粮食供应的增长。

sentences.en: This leads to competition and struggle for food and resources.
sentences.zh: 这导致了对食物和资源的竞争与争夺。

sentences.en: Not every individual can survive this competition.
sentences.zh: 并非每个个体都能在这场竞争中生存下来。

sentences.en: Darwin realized that in nature, animals and plants were also competing for limited resources.
sentences.zh: Darwin意识到，在大自然中，动植物同样在为有限的资源进行竞争。

sentences.en: Only those animals and plants with advantages, like stronger bodies, faster reactions, better camouflage, more efficient beaks, were more likely to survive and reproduce.
sentences.zh: 只有那些具备优势的动植物——比如更强壮的身体、更快的反应、更好的伪装、更高效的喙——才更有可能生存并繁殖后代。

sentences.en: Combining all of these ideas, Darwin developed the concept of natural selection.
sentences.zh: 结合所有这些想法，Darwin提出了自然选择的概念。

sentences.en: He proposed that individuals with traits better suited to their environment are more likely to survive and reproduce.
sentences.zh: 他提出，那些拥有更适合其环境特征的个体更有可能生存和繁殖。

sentences.en: Their advantages are passed on to the next generation.
sentences.zh: 它们的优势会被传递给下一代。

sentences.en: Over many generations, species gradually change.
sentences.zh: 经过许多代，物种逐渐发生了变化。

sentences.en: Species are not fixed or created exactly as they are forever.
sentences.zh: 物种并不是一成不变的，也不是被完美创造出来就永远保持原样的。

sentences.en: Instead, they evolve. And their evolution is influenced by the pressures of nature.
sentences.zh: 相反，它们在进化。并且它们的进化受到自然压力的影响。

sentences.en: Things like your predators, climate, food sources, diseases and competition.
sentences.zh: 比如捕食者、气候、食物来源、疾病和竞争等因素。

sentences.en: Those finches in the Galapagos Islands evolved differently.
sentences.zh: Galapagos群岛上的那些雀类就是以不同方式进化的。

sentences.en: On the island where the food source was hard seeds and nuts, birds with thicker, stronger beaks were more successful at eating and finding food.
sentences.zh: 在食物来源是坚硬的种子和坚果的岛上，喙更厚、更强壮的鸟类在进食和寻找食物方面更成功。

sentences.en: Hence, they gradually passed on those genetics.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们逐渐将这些基因遗传了下去。

sentences.en: On the other island, where the food sources were more to do with insects and cactus nectar, birds with longer beaks tended to do better, so eventually those birds developed long, thin beaks.
sentences.zh: 在另一个岛上，食物来源更多地与昆虫和仙人掌花蜜有关，喙更长的鸟类往往表现得更好，所以最终这些鸟类进化出了又长又细的喙。

sentences.en: This was a radical idea. It explained how new species could arise.
sentences.zh: 这是一个激进的想法。它解释了新物种是如何产生的。

sentences.en: It explained why fossils resembled some living animals.
sentences.zh: 它解释了为什么化石会酷似某些现存动物。

sentences.en: It explained why similar species lived in different places.
sentences.zh: 它解释了为什么相似的物种会生活在不同的地方。

sentences.en: And also why the Galapagos finches had different beaks.
sentences.zh: 同时也解释了为什么Galapagos雀类长着不同的喙。

sentences.en: Nature itself, over long stretches of time, was producing the diversity of life on Earth.
sentences.zh: 大自然本身在漫长的时间跨度里，创造了地球上生命的丰富多样性。

sentences.en: In 1858, a young naturalist named Alfred Russell Wallace sent Darwin an essay.
sentences.zh: 1858年，一位名叫Alfred Russell Wallace的年轻博物学家给Darwin寄了一篇论文。

sentences.en: Wallace, working completely independently in Southeast Asia, had developed a theory almost identical to Darwin’s.
sentences.zh: Wallace在东南亚完全独立地开展工作，也得出了几乎与Darwin相同的理论。

sentences.en: It was based on the same key idea. Species evolve through natural selection.
sentences.zh: 它基于同一个核心理念：物种通过自然选择进化。

sentences.en: Darwin was shocked. He had spent years building his case, his argument, but had never published anything, because he wanted more evidence and more proof first.
sentences.zh: Darwin大受震撼。他花了多年时间构建自己的论点和论据，却从未发表过任何内容，因为他想先获得更多证据和证明。

sentences.en: But now he risked being forgotten or overshadowed.
sentences.zh: 但现在他面临着被遗忘或被边缘化的风险。

sentences.en: To avoid conflict, both men agreed to present their ideas together to a scientific community.
sentences.zh: 为了避免冲突，两人同意将他们的观点共同提交给科学界。

sentences.en: And Darwin quickly finished his book. The following year, in 1859, he published On The Origin of Species, one of the most influential books in the history of science.
sentences.zh: Darwin迅速完成了他的书。第二年，即1859年，他出版了《物种起源》（On The Origin of Species），这是科学史上最具影响力的书籍之一。

sentences.en: Darwin’s writing was detailed, but clear and filled with evidence from nature.
sentences.zh: Darwin的著作详尽却清晰，充满了来自大自然的证据。

sentences.en: Some of his most important ideas included that all species, plants, animals, and humans as well are connected through shared ancestors.
sentences.zh: 他一些最重要的观点包括：所有物种（植物、动物，以及人类）都是通过共同的祖先联系在一起的。

sentences.en: The diversity of life we see today comes from millions of years of branching evolution.
sentences.zh: 我们今天看到的生命多样性来自数百万年的分支进化。

sentences.en: Evolution does not happen overnight. Species change slowly over long periods, across countless generations.
sentences.zh: 进化不是一夜之间发生的。物种在漫长的时间里、历经无数代缓慢地发生着变化。

sentences.en: And nature itself chooses which individuals survive and which individuals reproduce.
sentences.zh: 大自然本身选择了个体中哪些能够生存，哪些能够繁殖。

sentences.en: Those with beneficial traits are more likely to pass them on shaping the species over time.
sentences.zh: 那些拥有有益特征的个体更有可能将它们遗传下去，从而随着时间的推移塑造物种。

sentences.en: On the Origin of Species transformed biology.
sentences.zh: 《物种起源》彻底改变了生物学。

sentences.en: It provided a unifying explanation for many scientific mysteries like fossils, biodiversity, and the similarities among species.
sentences.zh: 它为化石、生物多样性以及物种间的相似性等许多科学谜题提供了一种统一的解释。

sentences.en: It paved the way for modern genetics, ecology, and even parts of medicine.
sentences.zh: 它为现代遗传学、生态学甚至是部分医学铺平了道路。

sentences.en: But it also sparked intense controversy, especially among religious communities.
sentences.zh: 但它也引发了激烈的争议，尤其是在宗教界。

sentences.en: Many people believe that species were fixed creations, designed exactly as they appeared.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为物种是固定不变的创造物，被设计成它们呈现出来的确切模样。

sentences.en: The idea that humans might share common ancestry with other animals was shocking, even offensive for some people.
sentences.zh: 人类可能与其他动物共享共同祖先的想法令人震惊，对某些人来说甚至具有冒犯性。

sentences.en: Darwin himself avoided discussing human evolution in detail in his book, but the implications were obvious.
sentences.zh: Darwin本人在书中避免详细讨论人类进化，但其中的含义是显而易见的。

sentences.en: Despite criticism, Darwin’s work spread rapidly.
sentences.zh: 尽管面临批评，Darwin的著作还是迅速传播开来。

sentences.en: Scientists and students debated his ideas passionately.
sentences.zh: 科学家和学生们热烈地辩论着他的观点。

sentences.en: While not everyone accepted evolution immediately, Darwin had set in motion a shift, a change, in how humans understand life.
sentences.zh: 虽然并非每个人都立刻接受了进化论，但Darwin已经引发了一场变革——人类理解生命方式的转变。

sentences.en: And science was never the same again. Charles Darwin’s ideas continue to influence almost every area of biology today.
sentences.zh: 科学从此再也不一样了。Charles Darwin的思想至今继续影响着当今生物学的几乎每一个领域。

sentences.en: His Theory of Evolution by natural selection is the foundation on which modern biology is built.
sentences.zh: 他的自然选择进化论是现代生物学建立的基石。

sentences.en: Without Darwin, our understanding of life on earth would be incomplete.
sentences.zh: 没有Darwin，我们对地球生命的理解将是不完整的。

sentences.en: Darwin, of course, worked without any knowledge of DNA or genetics.
sentences.zh: 当然，Darwin在工作时对DNA或遗传学一无所知。

sentences.en: This had not been discovered yet. He could not explain how traits were passed from parents to offspring.
sentences.zh: 这些当时尚未被发现。他无法解释特征是如何从父母传给后代的。

sentences.en: But decades later, scientists rediscovered the work of Gregor Mendel.
sentences.zh: 但几十年后，科学家们重新发现了Gregor Mendel的研究成果。

sentences.en: Mendel’s research on plants revealed the rules of inheritance.
sentences.zh: Mendel对植物的研究揭示了遗传规律。

sentences.en: Then eventually genetic science confirmed Darwin’s theory.
sentences.zh: 随后，遗传学最终证实了Darwin的理论。

sentences.en: DNA filled the gaps in Darwin’s understanding.
sentences.zh: DNA填补了Darwin认知中的空白。

sentences.en: DNA science showed that genes change over time, and those changes can create new traits.
sentences.zh: DNA科学表明基因会随着时间改变，而这些改变可以创造出新的特征。

sentences.en: Together evolution and genetics created the field now known as evolutionary biology.
sentences.zh: 进化论与遗传学结合在一起，催生了如今被称为进化生物学的领域。

sentences.en: Darwin’s ideas also affected medicine. Understanding evolution helps doctors now explain how viruses and bacteria adapts and how cancers evolve inside our bodies.
sentences.zh: Darwin的思想也影响了医学。理解进化论现在可以帮助医生解释病毒和细菌是如何适应环境的，以及癌症如何在我们的体内进化。

sentences.en: Darwin’s work also transformed how we study ecosystems and conservation, by showing that species are connected through ancestry and shaped by their environment.
sentences.zh: Darwin的工作还彻底改变了我们研究生态系统和保护工作的方式，它表明物种通过祖先相连并由环境塑造。

sentences.en: He helped scientists understand the delicate balance of nature.
sentences.zh: 他帮助科学家理解了大自然的微妙平衡。

sentences.en: Today, conservation efforts, including protecting endangered animals and restoring habitats, usually depends on evolutionary principles.
sentences.zh: 今天，包括保护濒危动物和恢复栖息地在内的保护工作，通常都依赖于进化原则。

sentences.en: Darwin also changed how humans, how we think about ourselves.
sentences.zh: Darwin还改变了人类看待自身、思考我们自己的方式。

sentences.en: His theory challenged the belief that humans are different from animals.
sentences.zh: 他的理论挑战了人类不同于动物的信仰。

sentences.en: Instead, we are part of the same family.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们是同一个大家庭的一部分。

sentences.en: More than 160 years after On the Origin of Species, Darwin’s theory remains one of the most powerful and tested ideas in all of science.
sentences.zh: 在《物种起源》出版160多年后，Darwin的理论依然是整个科学界最有力和经受住考验的思想之一。

sentences.en: Unlike many scientific theories that are replaced or rewritten, Darwin’s work has been consistently confirmed, strengthened and expanded.​
sentences.zh: 与许多被取代或重写的科学理论不同，Darwin的著作一直得到持续的证实、巩固和扩展。

sentences.en: After exploring Darwin’s life, his discovery and his enormous influence on modern science, we arrive at a big question.
sentences.zh: 在探索了Darwin的一生、他的发现以及他对现代科学的巨大影响之后，我们迎来了这样一个重大问题。

sentences.en: Was Charles Darwin the greatest scientist of all time?
sentences.zh: Charles Darwin是有史以来最伟大的科学家吗？

sentences.en: There are strong arguments in his favor.
sentences.zh: 有强有力的论据支持他。

sentences.en: Darwin changed how we understand life. His theory of evolution by natural selection created a framework that connects every field of biology.
sentences.zh: Darwin改变了我们对生命的理解。他的自然选择进化论创造了一个连接生物学各个领域的框架。

sentences.en: Very few scientific ideas have transformed our understanding of the world so completely.
sentences.zh: 很少有科学思想能如此彻底地改变我们对世界的理解。

sentences.en: However, some people argue that placing Darwin at the top is very difficult.
sentences.zh: 然而，有些人认为把Darwin排在第一位非常困难。

sentences.en: Science has many pioneers who shaped entire areas of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 科学界有许多塑造了整个知识领域的先驱。

sentences.en: Isaac Newton revolutionized physics, mathematics, and astronomy.
sentences.zh: Isaac Newton彻底革新了物理学、数学和天文学。

sentences.en: Einstein transformed our understanding of time, space, and energy.
sentences.zh: Einstein改变了我们对时间、空间和能量的理解。

sentences.en: Marie Skodowska Curie changed medicine and chemistry.
sentences.zh: Marie Skodowska Curie改变了医学和化学。

sentences.en: And people like Rosalind Franklin and others revealed the structure of DNA.
sentences.zh: Rosalind Franklin等其他人则揭示了DNA的结构。

sentences.en: Each of these scientists changed the world in their own ways.
sentences.zh: 这些科学家都以各自的方式改变了世界。

sentences.en: Should the greatest scientist be the one who explains the most important aspect of reality?
sentences.zh: 最伟大的科学家应该是一个解释了现实中最重要方面的人吗？

sentences.en: Or the one whose ideas affects our everyday lives?
sentences.zh: 还是那个其思想影响了我们日常生活的人？

sentences.en: I want to know your thoughts. Do you think Charles Darwin is the greatest scientist of all time?
sentences.zh: 我想知道你们的想法。你认为Charles Darwin是有史以来最伟大的科学家吗？

sentences.en: Who should I cover next in this series?
sentences.zh: 在这个系列里我接下来应该讲谁呢？
